Monica —

We just started seeing a spike in 5xx responses and a marked latency increase for production traffic routed to EastUS2 (our main region). Error rate jumped from ~0.4% to 7% between 07:45 and 08:00 UTC; several customer sessions dropped and we have multiple active incidents on our side. Attached a short log excerpt and a screenshot of our error-rate dashboard.

Key customer impact: large bot-scheduler job hitting generation endpoints times out and fails validation; two customers reported degraded throughput and request timeouts. This is P0 for us.

What we need: immediate mitigation (cross-region diversion to another region or an accelerated fallback plan) and an ETA on when EastUS2 will be healthy. Also please confirm whether Redwood can enable a temporary traffic steer and whether any model-variant compatibility concerns exist.

Attaching: server_logs_20280615.txt, err_rate_screenshot_0615.png

— Ena

On Fri, Jun 15, 2028 at 08:25 Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the quick heads-up and logs. We’re treating this as a P0.

Summary of findings (initial):
- Telemetry shows KV cache saturation and a downstream node replication lag in EastUS2-A starting ~07:40 UTC. The saturation manifests as increased tail latency and cascading 5xx on generation endpoints for long-context sessions.
- No config rollouts were active during the window; this appears infra-side.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Runtime steering: update routing policy to divert NeonRise production routes from EastUS2 -> WestUS2. WestUS2 has compatible GPU pool and model variants for NeonRise. Estimated impact: 2–4 minutes to apply + up to 90s for warmed cache on WestUS2 for long-context workloads.
2) Model-variant fallback: move to a lower-kv-dependency variant (memory-friendly quantized variant) for NeonRise traffic in EastUS2 while we heal. Expected quality delta small for your workloads but measurable.
3) Request priority capacity on Dedicated pool if NeonRise wants reserved throughput to avoid repeated cross-region moves.

I recommend option (1) now to stop customer impact, followed by (2) if we see residual errors after steer. I’ve attached the reroute checklist and a short runbook extract for the cut.

Action items assigned:
- Monica: please confirm authorization to perform runtime steering.
- Ena: confirm whether NeonRise expects any session-affinity constraints.
- Hannah: stand by to monitor post-steer metrics and initiate rollback if error rate increases on target region.

Attachments: reroute-playbook.pdf

— Rishi

Markus —

Looping you in given this is a P0 for a high-value strategic account (Deal DL-4721). We have an active incident in EastUS2 causing 5–7% 5xx and tail latency spikes. Rishi recommends immediate runtime steering to WestUS2 to stop customer impact; this requires exec sign-off for a temporary cross-region diversion plus authorization for any credit/SLA accommodations should NeonRise ask.

Context: NeonRise ops reported the spike at 08:12 UTC. We can flip routing within minutes and expect most client sessions to recover; however, long-context sessions may see transient failures while KV caches warm in WestUS2. We have a pagerduty incident open (PD-89321).

Request: please approve an exec bridge now (15–30min) and confirm we can sign off on a temporary diversion. If approved, I’ll coordinate the bridge URL and call the cut.
